Anybody who does a herioc act is and forever will be considered a hero. Heroes are not defined by how much they do, but what they do. "A World of Heroes" reveals the following: "As the jet began a rapid dive over New York City, Sullenberger remained calm...and landed it on the Hudson River" (6-7). A hero's identity doesn't come from the quantity of his actions, but the impact of those actions which help others, big or small, just as Sullenberger did. Anyone is considered a hero if he is brave, courageous, and helps others in need. "A World of Heroes" mentions "The monumental response of volunteers immediately following the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001" (7). Volunteers risked their lives to help out citizens in need. Heroes are defined by the brave and courageous actions they take to help others, regardless of putting their own life in danger, just like the 9/11 volunteers did.

     On the contrary, heroes need to do many repeated heroic deeds to be considered a hero. The title "hero" is an extraordinary achievement for someone to be rewarded with, so it requires a plethora of heroic deeds in order to be rewarded that title. Beowulf states, "Crying that no better king had ever/Lived/.../so deserving of praise" (865 and 867). Beowulf was a great leader who gained his heroic title from the countless monsters he slayed. If people who are brave, courageous, and help others are considered heroes, then almost anyone can be a hero. However, being a hero is defined by the impact and importance of an action, not how many times someone repeats it. Doing a single selfless act like protecting someone getting bullied or saving a life shows characteristics of a true hero. By calling someone a hero by how many acts they do, it's not fair to those who put their life in danger to save someone one time. Anyone who does a courageous act that helps others defines what a hero should be.

When deciding if sacrifice or success is the bigger contributor to heroism, sacrifice is a more definitive term for someone's act of heroism because a person's dedication and rejection to look at the negative outcomes is more important than winning a battle. A person's dedication to the point of death rather surpasses staying alive and succeeding. This is because people need a brave hero unafraid of death and willing to protect others, and don't need a person who thinks they are a hero because they think they can win every battle as a result of winning one or more battles in the past. Succession is a weak mindset, and the people who believe in it will not be any kind of hero because they don't realize that no hero has ever succeeded every time. In Beowulf, Beowulf reveals his strong mindset of sacrifice saying, " I mean not to stand, not run from his shooting / Flames, stand till fate decides / Which of us wins" (635-637). This quote perfectly explains what kind of mindset divides a true hero's dedication, brave and unphased with the thought of sacrificing oneself, and a weak hero's dedication, fearful of death and thinks that winning comes easy. Reasoning that success is better than sacrifice isn't a terrible argument because the argument that having a bunch of victories could be more frightening to the opponent, but this is not true. The only frightening thing when battling is who is scared of certain aspects of war and who isn't afraid of anything, including something as horrifying as death. The people who aren't afraid of anything are the real heroes because they show that they care for what they are fighting for that they do not hesitate to die for others.

     Another reason that also comes with dedication is looking past and ignoring all negative outcomes of war. When a hero's mindset is so focused on what they are fighting for that they look past all negative outcomes, put their life on the line, and die for their reasons shows to other people their dedication. Leading by example is also very important, and when a hero shows their peers how to act brave and only focus on the war, it forms a society of people who are unafraid and willing to take your place if you die. This is how strong cities or countries are formed, not by winning a lot, but by having one hero to be a role model and lead by example on how to act in war and how your mindset makes you stronger than the opponent. Beowulf reveals "We shall see, soon, who will survive / This bloody battle, stand when the fighting / Is done" (Beowulf 640-643). In this quote, it is referring to Beowulf speaking to the people of his city that he rules over. He is explaining to them that this last battle may be the battle that ends his legacy and more importantly his life, so he tells them just to be prepared to step in for him and to train the army as he fought and how he showed them to fight for so long as their king. This is why sacrifice is a better characteristic to describe a hero than success.

Taking a stand counts more than winning. When it comes to being a hero, bravery is crucial factor. Having the bravery to take a stand and do what you can is important. It's not about just defeating the scariest enemy or solving the biggest crime, but about having the resolve to do what others won't and try. One cannot hope to win a battle if they haven't begun to fight. A World of Heros shows bravery. "As the jet began a rapid dive over New York City, Sullenburger remained calm, kept steady, and landed it on the Hudson River"(7). Imagine if Chesley Sullenberger hadn't stepped up and decided to panic like the rest of the plane. Every passenger that was on that plane more than likely would have died.

 Taking a stand can not only give you courage, but it can inspre those around you to do the same. When seeing a person who's desperately trying to help even though everyone else is only watching, people can band together to help out because it only takes one persons heroic action, to influence the actions of many. However, this is not always the case. In the epic Beowulf, when it was time to fight the dragon, Beowulf's subordinates were not moved by the actions of they're king. Instead, they fled him and the kingdom when they were needed to help. Fear overcame them and made them even seeing someones brave actions to fight, that is why courage is a crucial factor. This one instance does not mean taking a stand is less important. No matter the outcome of that choice people will still remember that someone was brave enough to try, and that will stay in their minds forever.

Taking a stand is more important than winning; because, you need to take to a stand to win. Different adjectives arise when you think of heroes such as: loyal, selfless and brave. When he fights Grendel in his first battle, he uses nothing but grit and determination. His next battle is a little different. Beowulf, swims down deep into Grendel's mother's liar, which was described as "burning like a torch." At some points in this battle, there are times where Beowulf seems like he will lose, but finds a way. Beowulf has super-strength, power over the Danes, and is honored around England as a hero. 

 

However, some people will tell you, "heroes are only in fiction." But let's think to different times in hisotry where regular, everday people, became heroes. In the article, "A World of Heroes" there are different situations that saw everyday show heroic traits. January 15th, 2009, Chesley Sullenberger's plane was struck by a flock of geese, which saw the engines malfunction. In the 3rd paragraph, it states, "Sullenberger remained calm, kept the plane steady, and landed on the Hudson River. He didn't need super strength as Beowulf possesed, but he did show bravery. There are so many people in the universe and each one of them can be a hero, it doesn't need to be someone with super strength or any supernatural abilites. Just someone who shows an act of bravery, loyalty, and wasn't the king of Denmark, yet he's considered a hero. Anyone in the world can be a hero, but only by taking a stand.
